canal_p16_001.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_001.text: On the thirty-seventh morning, the market opened on the higher landing instead of the lower square. A woman sold hot rice beside a stack of closed cargo baskets. Children watched the recovered branch laid on its sound edge, disappointed that it looked like ordinary wet wood after frightening so many adults. Yue bought breakfast before opening the loss-review sheet. The smell of ginger and cooking oil made the work feel stranger than the storm had. People were already trying to live in the space after danger, while its costs still waited unnamed.

canal_p16_002.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_002.text: The gardener brought the actual crop inspection, his saved-basket sales and the planting receipts in three different wrappers. He had slept badly and snapped at his daughter for folding one corner incorrectly. She gave him the right wrapper and went to buy her own breakfast. Yue waited until he noticed she had left. He called after her and apologized without explaining the flood first. His losses were real. They had not acquired a right to take every smaller person's morning along with them.

canal_p16_003.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_003.text: The reed gatherer had counted the torn sailcloth roof and the ruined small bedding roll left beneath it. His cutter stayed dry in the higher shed, and his spoon had returned. He wanted the damaged cloth priced as the material he actually used, not a new elegant shelter nobody had ever seen him own. Yue asked for his ordinary repairer's quote. He had brought it, folded under the spoon. The object he most wanted back now helped hold evidence of things whose loss could be purchased at an ordinary price.

canal_p16_004.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_004.text: The food-stall owner arrived with the batch record she gave Luo during the gate closure. Some prepared food had spoiled when customers did not come, though she sold other portions at a lower price. She wanted the actual lost stock and canceled bookings heard. The ledger did not promise repayment of every imagined traveler. Yue compared her offered record with the current closure times. The woman disliked the reduced count, then admitted one hoped-for boat had never booked a meal. That hope still hurt, but she took it out of the direct-loss line.

canal_p16_005.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_005.text: Pei arranged the fortieth-day hearing copies on the counter and asked claimants to read their own offered accounts before she made the public packet. Private household cupboards stayed outside it. Yue carried the gardener's approved loss count to the receiving clerk after he corrected one planting date. The younger daughter had remembered that date from the stick tally. Her father named her method in the account. An angry man could become more accurate without becoming cheerful, and Yue was learning to wait for that smaller change.

canal_p16_006.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_006.text: Bao went to the ordinary clinician because wrist pain persisted through light grip. The examination found continuing sprain signs, with no new reason to abandon the supported rest plan; a worsening symptom would require referral. His private household paid this actual follow-up charge from its ordinary funds after Han's offered first visit payment. Han's one copper had not bought unlimited medical care or settled every consequence. Bao kept the restriction and sent Luo his actual availability for later light observation, declining loaded tools.

canal_p16_007.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_007.text: Tian visited him with the gate seedling in its stable pot, then took it home before the wind changed. Bao said the plant had a better repair schedule than his wrist. Tian said it also refused to use a hammer, an example he might consider. He laughed and asked whether she could stitch a support strap to the clinician's ordinary specification. She quoted the small private work and waited for him to accept. The friendship made joking possible. It did not turn her skill into a new free service.

canal_p16_008.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_008.text: The garden owner's mason completed the two floorboard replacement and ordinary drying tasks through the separately paid property appointment. The tenant's sleeping platform passed its receiving check on the thirty-eighth morning if the drying interval held. The paid higher lodging already covered that night. The grandmother wanted the wet herbs discarded only after she identified which jars remained usable. The owner arranged a safe reachable inspection rather than declaring the whole kitchen clean because the floor now looked better from the doorway.

canal_p16_009.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_009.text: At Han's dry store table, the conservator inspected the damp personal paper bundle under a separately priced private appointment. Some pages could be eased apart after controlled drying; others had already lost portions of ink. He would preserve what remained rather than rewrite missing sentences from Han's memory. Yue watched the shoes dry on their cloth and understood that the chest could return while its contents remained partly gone. Han chose the limited treatment and paid its actual small first fee from ordinary store receipts.

canal_p16_010.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_010.text: One recovered sheet named the cost of the canceled shop extension. Han read it and said his mother had expected the larger building to make his adult life easier. The hoist and spare planks reserved for the cooper came from that unbuilt plan. Selling them now felt less like clearing stock than changing the future she had imagined. Yue asked whether keeping them unused made that future arrive. He said no, impatiently, then apologized because she had not meant the question as a lesson.

canal_p16_011.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_011.text: The conservator found a half-legible household line beside the extension cost. Han thought it said the family should never forgive the bank for late payments. The missing middle could not establish that sentence. He left his interpretation in a private memory note, separate from the recovered ink. The public fifty-six claim had its intact certified records elsewhere. Yue was relieved that his private grief no longer had to turn every damaged word into authority over the canal. It could remain grief, harder to settle and less dangerous to other people's days.

canal_p16_012.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_012.text: The private buyer's agent sent a reminder that the forty-eight deposit return remained due by the review term's end. Han's thirty-two was still set aside, and the cooper's sixteen receiving payment remained booked for day forty. The flood had left the reserved surplus goods dry. Han wanted the agent to recognize his private repair costs as another reason to wait longer. The contract's existing period still allowed the planned settlement; no extension had been granted. Yue helped compare the actual terms he offered, leaving his wish visible without writing it as an agreement.

canal_p16_013.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_013.text: At the lower return, the public officer documented the accessible clay displacement and branch obstruction after the fall. The present route report showed where observed water pooled and where the clearing changed its level. It did not alone measure every person's loss or decide the quarry owner's fault. The officer would provide the actual public portions for the hearing. Yue put the receiving time beside the crop count, grateful for evidence that could be useful without pretending it already answered every angry question in the market.

canal_p16_014.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_014.text: The quarry owner replied through his current verified business receiver. He offered the storage bank's permit drawing and said he had hired a builder to keep carts dry. Its terms required the ordinary outlet remain unobstructed, with a defined storage footprint. The officer's current report described narrowing at that outlet and held runoff before the slump. Comparing the actual work with the permit would need its own inspection and reply process. Luo received the offered paper without letting a sealed drawing become proof the work had followed it.

canal_p16_015.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_015.text: One trustee wanted to announce the quarry owner responsible for all damage below the fork. The gardener said that would make his claim easier. The garden owner asked whether it would also explain the old slide and blocked return. Yue read the dated observations in order, including the maintained preparations and stopped low trial. The trustee withdrew the complete statement and asked for a scoped investigation of the bank and outlet. It was less satisfying in the room, but it gave the owner a question he could actually answer.

canal_p16_016.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_016.text: The landing guild's winter store keeper brought a count of twelve available standard grain sacks, ten kilograms each, set aside for temporary relief to three working households whose verified losses had interrupted ordinary income. The gardener, reed gatherer and food-stall household had requested that support. The guild trustees authorized four sacks offered to each from this separate one-hundred-twenty-kilogram stock. The thirty-six emergency cash had already bought its own response. Food support would not be drawn from the remaining charge, Han's deposit envelope or a future monthly toll share.

canal_p16_017.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_017.text: The recipients could accept the actual offered food without making it full compensation or assigning their current work to the guild. One trustee wanted signatures promising a season of future common service. Tian pointed to the canceled successor notice still visible beside the counter. The chair removed that added condition before the offer went out. The guild could hire future workers under real terms. Its food did not need to plant the same old obligation in a new household cupboard.

canal_p16_018.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_018.text: The grain store opened after authorization. Its keeper checked the sacks' labels and condition before receiving carts took them. Yue counted their standard weights on the checked scale. One sack was a kilogram short after grain escaped through a worn seam. The shortage stayed in the guild's stock-loss account. The keeper filled it from three kilograms already counted in the separate loose bin, leaving two there, then sealed the full offered quantity. The recipients would receive one hundred twenty actual kilograms, rather than symbolic sacks made lighter by everybody's hurry.

canal_p16_019.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_019.text: The gardener accepted his four sacks for household food, keeping them distinct from damaged crop seed. The store grain had its ordinary food label and no seed qualification. He would buy replacement seed through its own checked source if that later became his choice. His daughter asked whether they could plant the little saved bean. The experienced grower would assess it before any use. Yue kept the two supplies separate while the family cart received forty kilograms of actual food. The acceptance did not remove their claim for the flooded bed.

canal_p16_020.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_020.text: The reed gatherer wanted two sacks immediately and the other two held for collection when he moved from the higher shed. The store keeper accepted that recorded receiving arrangement, with his chosen pickup time and counterpart. Forty kilograms remained his offered relief allocation; twenty had actually departed so far. Yue wrote the difference. He thanked her for not making him carry more than his cart could take. A generous quantity could still become difficult if the receiving plan imagined a stronger vehicle than the one at the door.

canal_p16_021.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_021.text: The food-stall owner accepted her four sacks for household meals, not as stock she must sell cheaply to repay the guild. She kept the direct spoilage claim and her ordinary future business. The guild store gave her the food label and actual receiving note. A neighbor said she ought to cook a free public feast after such a gift. She said she would offer a paid rice pot at tomorrow's market if people wanted it. Yue smiled at the ordinary answer, which let gratitude exist without turning a working hearth into another public obligation.

canal_p16_022.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_022.text: By afternoon, ten of the twelve accepted relief sacks had left under their actual receiving notes, while two remained assigned for the gatherer's later collection. The store's loose-bin top-up and worn-seam loss stayed accounted separately. The guild still held title to unoffered winter stock; nothing had been promised beyond the twelve authorized sacks. Yue put the completed food receipts beside the proposed later loss decisions. A measured meal supply could ease the week without pretending it returned drowned beans, torn roofs or every canceled fare.

canal_p16_023.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_023.text: The cart driver who crossed the foot-only board came to the counter with Han. He admitted the wrong route and asked for the actual public repair expense caused by that crossing. The emergency record identified its limited shoulder repair, separate from later flood displacement. Han offered to reimburse the verified one-copper material use from his private cart service receipts. The council accepted it into the maintenance reserve and left the emergency purchase account's original expenditure visible. The returned copper would not be silently counted twice as both unspent response and new income.

canal_p16_024.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_024.text: The driver's labor incident note kept his mistake without imposing an invented wage penalty. Han would revise the private cart route briefing, with the driver reading back its load limits before another service. The actual reimbursement came from private service receipts, outside the thirty-two reserved for deposit return. Yue watched the driver sign and noticed how relieved he looked after the expense became specific. Responsibility had felt limitless while people argued about what might have happened. One observed wrong crossing now had one actual repair payment and one changed procedure.

canal_p16_025.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_025.text: An ordinary messenger brought Ren Qiao's orchard reply note to Yue after the market closed. The matron had received the requested third morning after canal closure, but needed to confirm the actual patient and staff availability before accepting it. The retained earlier arrangement remained distinct from a universal return promise. Any personal visit still owed had not been completed by this reply. Ren asked whether Yue could allow the appointment its full current review interval. Yue checked her closing itinerary and wrote a real answer through her paid personal message route.

canal_p16_026.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_026.text: Tian asked whether another request would make Yue postpone the canal's ending again. Yue said she wanted the matron's actual accepted day after closure, with a booked ordinary journey funded from earned wages. She would not stay indefinitely beside the lock because leaving felt less flattering than being useful. Tian said she should also leave room to eat. They shared the market's remaining ginger rice, bought at its actual late price. The overdue visit had begun changing Yue's calendar before anybody pretended a letter had cured it.

canal_p16_027.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_027.text: Three preparation tasks remained for the fortieth-day loss hearing. The gardener and stall owner wanted their actual accounts compared with received observations; Pei needed the completed relief receiving notes assembled without treating food as settlement; Han wanted his private reimbursed crossing and prospective goods delivery kept distinct from the public claims. The clerk would gather every result. Yue could work beside loss, beside temporary support or beside responsibility accepted by someone she had spent much of the term opposing.

canal_p16_028.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_028.text: The recovered personal papers lay drying at Han's table while the public hearing copies waited at the counter. Yue felt the temptation to make the week tell one clean story: common water rescued, private overreach corrected, relief delivered. The real people had crops still missing, a wrist still painful, a chest partly damaged and a promised visit still waiting for a day its recipient could accept. The next task would decide which of those unfinished matters she understood best when they finally sat down to hear claims.

canal_p16_029.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_029.text: Yue could compare actual losses with their observed route, assemble the separate grain relief receiving account or help Han prepare the limited private responsibility and delivery record. The food would remain support rather than a purchase of future household work. The deposit return would still need sixteen actual copper on day forty. The hearing could use honest incomplete records instead of forcing every open question to look solved before its owners entered the room.

choices.text: Compare offered losses with current observations.
Assemble the separate grain receiving account.
Prepare Han's limited private responsibility and delivery record.

canal_p16_030.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_030.text: The gardener opened his planting book beside the stall owner's batch notes. Their losses had different kinds of evidence. His work stretched across seasons; her spoiled rice existed for hours. Yue asked each to describe what the current document could count before comparing money. The gardener wanted a future market price for every bent plant. The stall owner wanted the actual purchase and preparation cost of portions no longer safe to sell. Their claims could be heard together without pretending the same calculation served both.

canal_p16_031.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_031.text: The experienced grower's field note distinguished salvageable dirty pods from food that should be discarded under ordinary quality checks. The gardener disliked the smaller lost count until his daughter asked whether keeping good pods meant another paid sorting day. It might, if a real order justified the work and somebody accepted the terms. Yue put that possible future job outside the present loss total. Salvage was an actual resource, but an unbooked sale could not enter the account as money already earned.

canal_p16_032.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_032.text: The gardener's higher saved baskets had brought a lower storm-week price than he expected. That price loss belonged to a different line from the crop physically ruined. A trader who had paid the actual amount offered the receiving note for comparison. Yue asked the family whether it could enter the hearing copy. They agreed to the quantity and price, keeping another private customer line covered. The claim grew more precise, which made it easier for a distant trustee to see why a healthy-looking basket did not mean nothing had been lost.

canal_p16_033.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_033.text: The food-stall owner had carried one cooking pot to the higher market and sold ginger rice there. Her actual sales reduced the spoiled-stock loss, but had not replaced every canceled lower-square meal. She wanted the hearing to hear the extra fuel and carrying work too. Yue asked for their actual paid quantities and the worker's chosen account. A neighbor had helped carry the pot as a gift and declined a wage claim. The owner could name that help without converting it into an expense nobody had actually paid.

canal_p16_034.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_034.text: The temporary check worker's changed income appeared in the same packet. He had accepted two occasional upstream shifts, both complete, while the old repeated gate checks would shrink after the repair term. The saved public cost was real, and so was his reduced recurring wage opportunity. His current statement asked for future task notices and a chance to apply for genuine work, not cash for every imagined night. Yue kept the actual accepted upstream wages separate. The hearing would have a person after the gate improvement, not just the improvement's savings.

canal_p16_035.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_035.text: At the counter, a trustee objected to hearing lost opportunities beside direct damage. The chair said the records would distinguish them without refusing people whose consequences did not fit the simplest cost column. The gardener said he wished his beans had been only an opportunity. The worker said he wished his lost checks had been only an accounting saving. Their rough exchange made Yue uneasy, then both men laughed at comparing which kind of loss sounded easier when described by somebody else.

canal_p16_036.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_036.text: The garden tenant's offered household account named the wet mat, spoiled herbs and temporary displacement. Her replacement millet and painted cup had stayed dry; the original loss from the previous season remained under its private settlement. Yue compared the dates to keep this flood from swallowing the earlier agreement or being charged twice for the same millet. The grandmother read the result and said it was strange to be grateful for a neat date. The date protected a small real mercy from being turned into another argument.

canal_p16_037.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_037.text: The owner had paid extra lodging and accepted the two-board private repair. Those received costs could appear in her separate offered property claim without charging the tenant for work needed before the room resumed service. Yue asked both women to read the overlap line. They agreed that the direct landlord payment did not remove every later question about the spill route. The account kept their private action visible, useful to the hearing without treating one good decision as a certificate of all future kindness.

canal_p16_038.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_038.text: The gardener asked whether accepting forty kilograms of relief food would reduce his crop claim automatically. The offer expressly preserved claims, and the actual receiving note showed food support without a settlement condition. Yue put that document beside his own account. Any later negotiated credit would need his actual agreement rather than a trustee's convenient subtraction. He said he wanted to be helped without being told the help proved he had enough. Yue nodded, hearing a familiar fear from someone who had opposed the canal.

canal_p16_039.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_039.text: Yue finished the comparative loss packet with direct damage, actual price changes and future work consequences stated separately. The offered sources and remaining inspections stayed visible. The hearing receiver would use it on day forty, with each claimant able to answer its own lines. The gardener and stall owner left without promising to agree about common use. Their accounts no longer had to compete for one vague word called suffering. Yue took a deep breath and folded the packet, grateful for the ordinary limit of a page she could actually carry.

canal_p16_040.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_040.text: The guild store keeper showed Yue the food receiving ledger before opening the loose-bin cover. The authorized relief was twelve ten-kilogram sacks. A one-kilogram shortage in the worn sack had been filled from three kilograms already counted in the loose bin, leaving two there outside this offer. The spoiled or lost storage grain stayed in its actual stock-loss entry. Ten accepted sacks had departed, and two were held for the gatherer's chosen collection. The numbers told a small concrete story of food still waiting.

canal_p16_041.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_041.text: The gatherer arrived with his ordinary cart after clearing the higher shed's access. He could carry the remaining two sacks under its present load. The keeper weighed and released their twenty kilograms against the earlier forty-kilogram allocation, recording the second receiving time. All twelve authorized sacks had now departed in actual full quantities. Yue watched him tuck the counterpart beside his spoon. The spoon made him smile; the grain would make the week easier. Neither pretended to buy his roof or future labor.

canal_p16_042.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_042.text: The store keeper asked whether the held sacks could have been given to another family before the gatherer returned. The accepted offer and recorded pickup kept them assigned to him. A changed need could be proposed, but his collection arrangement had not become abandonment. Yue read the counterpart aloud while the keeper made the final entry. The gatherer heard and thanked them. She remembered the valley's empty absent-claims column and was glad this ordinary waiting quantity had remained somebody's real food.

canal_p16_043.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_043.text: At the higher market, the food-stall owner cooked from her separate business stock rather than the household relief sacks. She wanted the offer's food used for home meals and the public rice pot priced through its own ordinary costs. A customer joked that the guild had already paid for everyone's supper. The woman showed the menu and told him where the accepted support actually went. He paid for a bowl. Yue bought one too, enjoying ginger without asking the relief ledger to explain every grain at the hearth.

canal_p16_044.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_044.text: The gardener's household moved its received sacks into a dry corner above the reopened foot route. His daughter wrote the food label in broad letters and set the possible seed bean elsewhere. An uncle wanted to scatter the store grain in the damaged bed to see what grew. The gardener stopped him before he wasted it. The food sacks were not tested seed. Yue laughed when the daughter announced that one tiny bean now had more important qualifications than forty kilograms of rice.

canal_p16_045.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_045.text: The guild chair read the relief offer again before signing the completed receiving account. Its support did not settle damage claims or require future household turns. The proposed service condition removed before delivery remained visible in the meeting note, so a later copy would not quietly restore it. Yue asked whether leaving the rejected line invited another argument. The chair said it showed what they had actually refused. A generous-looking clean copy could become dangerous if people forgot why one tempting sentence had been crossed out.

canal_p16_046.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_046.text: The store keeper's assistant wanted a public list of recipients as thanks for the guild. The recipients had approved the actual aggregate relief account and their own chosen acknowledgments, not a display of private need at the market. Yue carried those preferences to the keeper. The public notice could show twelve sacks, one hundred twenty kilograms and completed delivery without treating every household kitchen as evidence of the trustees' generosity. The assistant rewrote it plainly and asked the recipients how they preferred their counterparts kept.

canal_p16_047.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_047.text: The reed gatherer chose to name his received quantity publicly because he wanted other seasonal workers to know they could ask for support under real terms. The stall owner preferred the aggregate account; the gardener allowed his food receipt in his hearing packet. Their different choices did not change the measured delivery. Yue gave each its own receiving path. The support felt more common when it did not demand one public posture from everybody whose cart left the same door.

canal_p16_048.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_048.text: A child asked the keeper whether the loose-bin's remaining two kilograms belonged to nobody. He said it stayed guild winter stock under its ordinary account. She wanted to feed all of it to the keeper's goose. Yue thought Luo's geese would approve the proposal. The keeper gave the child a small measured scoop from his own animal feed tin instead, after her parent agreed. Public grain kept its assigned purpose, and the goose got breakfast from a person who actually owned the offered feed.

canal_p16_049.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_049.text: At the counter, Yue delivered the completed twelve-sack receiving account after the gatherer's second collection. One hundred twenty kilograms had reached the three accepted recipients, with the worn-seam top-up and remaining loose stock separately recorded. The public version followed their offered preferences. The food support stayed alongside unfinished claims. Yue had spent the afternoon moving nothing heavier than paper and still felt the weight of quantities that could disappear when a clerk called a held sack unneeded or a gift a debt.

canal_p16_050.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_050.text: Han showed Yue the actual one-copper reimbursement receiving note at his private store. The public reserve had received it for the limited material use caused by the wrong cart crossing. The emergency's original eight-copper material expenditure stayed visible in that closed account. The driver would read back the corrected foot and cart routes before his next private shift. Han asked whether that was enough to make the incident stop following him. Yue said it completed this agreed repair payment, which was an answer less magical than the one he wanted.

canal_p16_051.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_051.text: The driver came with the new route sheet and his own actual cart load note. Han had corrected the turning path around the private platform rather than simply printing the warning larger. Yue walked its reachable dry section with them under the current public access limit. The driver read the intended level route aloud and pointed to the foot-only crossing he would avoid. Han accepted the briefing before booking another customer. The change involved a real path, not merely a document designed to look better at the hearing.

canal_p16_052.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_052.text: At the high store, the reserved hoist and four planks remained sound and dry under the current inspection. The cooper's receiving installer would check them after delivery on day forty as part of the ordinary private purchase arrangement. Bao's injured wrist supplied no fresh private certification. Han had the earlier inspected report and present storage condition. Yue helped read the goods tags from the dry side while the store worker compared them with the contract. The intended sixteen remained promised until those actual receiving checks passed.

canal_p16_053.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_053.text: Han asked whether the cooper might reduce his price because the flood had hurt other business. The purchase terms fixed twelve for the hoist and four for the planks, conditional on their actual specified condition. A changed opinion about the canal did not change the accepted price on its own. The goods could still fail a real check, which would need an actual reply. Yue read that condition with him. He looked relieved by the ordinary shape of a risk that had not yet become another surprise.

canal_p16_054.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_054.text: The private delivery cart would take the checked upper route and stay within its own load allowance. Han's current store cash paid the booked carriage separately from the thirty-two deposit envelope and the expected sixteen receiving payment. The cooper's installer appointment belonged to the buyer's own ordinary business. Yue wanted the account to remain simple, then saw that simplicity would hide two real private costs. Han showed both receiving arrangements willingly. He had begun understanding that naming a cost did not automatically invite the canal to pay it.

canal_p16_055.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_055.text: The buyer's agent sent acknowledgment of the day-forty delivery plan but demanded a firm remittance date for the deposit. Han offered the forty-first day if the cooper actually paid, within the existing review-term deadline. The agent accepted that conditional notice date without granting an extension or treating the payment complete. Yue kept the two statements beside each other. A plan could be specific and still depend on a receipt. The important change was that Han now told the agent exactly which dependency remained.

canal_p16_056.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_056.text: Han opened the drying personal paper bundle only at the conservator's next instructed stage. One page separated cleanly; another stayed joined along a damaged edge. He wanted to peel it faster and remembered Bao's wrist when his own fingers trembled. Yue asked whether he wanted the conservator called again. He said yes and set the sheet down. The private old chest had not become less personal because a careful method delayed it. It had become personal enough to deserve a method that did not make his urgency destroy more words.

canal_p16_057.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_057.text: The store worker read a recovered extension cost line at Han's invitation and asked whether selling the planks meant the canceled larger shop would never happen. Han said it would require a new decision and new funds, not the unused stock already promised to the cooper. The worker wanted future shifts, but not another uncertain project disguised as available wages. Han agreed to post actual openings when they existed. Yue heard an echo of Tian's job board without another lecture about the old pledge.

canal_p16_058.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_058.text: Tian brought the repaired coat's receiving note to the young worker and Han after its ordinary agreed payment. The worker wore the patch inside, as chosen, and tested the hem around his boots. He wanted the next loading list to mark upper-room returns separately from goods completion. Han had done that and showed the actual changed form. Yue watched the man read his own future task copy. The rescue had left something more practical than thanks: one worker could now tell whether his employer knew he came back.

canal_p16_059.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_059.text: At the counter, Yue submitted the limited public reimbursement, revised private cart route and conditional goods delivery plan. Han kept his private originals and the thirty-two set aside. The public hearing would hear his actual responsibility for the crossing without using it to erase his fifty-six toll claim or invent ownership over his other employees. The next private receiving check would decide whether sixteen new copper arrived. Yue felt unexpectedly protective of that distinction for a man whose first notice had tried to deny it to Tian.

canal_p16_060.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_060.text: By evening, the three preparation packets reached their actual receivers. The losses carried measured claims and open cause questions, the grain support had twelve full sacks actually delivered and Han's private incident had its limited payment and changed route. Yue had followed one set of conversations closely. The others spoke for their own completed work. The fortieth-day hearing could now begin from changed facts, rather than spend its whole first hour proving that the storm happened and everybody had suffered in the same way.

canal_p16_061.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_061.text: On the thirty-eighth morning, the property mason accepted the dried sleeping platform and repaired lower boards under the owner's separate job. The grandmother could resume ordinary light use through the checked door, with the heavy grain tub moved only after the floor's load allowance permitted it. The paid lodging had covered the prior night and ended at its agreed time. Her host gave the receiving note without adding future favors to it. Yue helped carry the light sack back on the actual open route and watched the painted cup find its familiar table.

canal_p16_062.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_062.text: The grandmother asked Yue to leave the recovered stool where her husband used to sit. Its feet had been checked dry after the flood, and one still wobbled on the uneven board. Her son wanted to plane it immediately. She preferred a little ordinary felt pad until the carpenter could assess whether the stool or floor caused the movement. Bao would not be summoned with his sprained wrist. The owner found a household pad, and the stool settled. A small stable seat had required no new power.

canal_p16_063.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_063.text: The gardener finished sorting safe salvage through an actual paid afternoon agreed with his neighbor. The direct sorting wage came from his current private crop receipts, not the relief food or public repair purse. Some dirty pods failed their ordinary sale check and stayed discarded. He counted the resulting safe sale quantity separately from lost yield. Yue took the offered receiving figures for the hearing after he approved them. The harvest had survived partly, and that partial survival still required somebody's real work before it became money.

canal_p16_064.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_064.text: The stall owner kept her new market batch smaller because customer traffic remained uncertain. She sold nearly all of it, then closed before making an optimistic second pot. Yue bought the last bowl with Tian and asked whether she wanted the actual successful batch in her offered update. She did. It showed the business adapting without canceling its earlier verified spoilage. Tian said a repaired seam also had to keep working after someone admired it. The owner laughed and asked whether Tian could mend her apron at an ordinary price next week.

canal_p16_065.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_065.text: The reed gatherer returned to the old camp during controlled access and chose a modest roof patch through his regular repairer's actual quote. His temporary higher shed space had reached its stated end; he would use an offered private sleeping corner at a cousin's home until the roof's receiving check. The cousin offered two nights without a charge after asking what he needed. The guild's food remained his household supply, not a reason to demand a larger public room. Yue recorded the completed shed return only after his cutter moved out safely.

canal_p16_066.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_066.text: The quarry owner attended the public officer's scoped outlet inspection through his actual current receiver. The report found the permitted storage footprint had been narrowed in one place by an added stack, reducing the ordinary outlet's accessible width. The owner said his builder had misunderstood the marked line. The officer preserved that reply and measured the current work. Responsibility and remedies would need the proper review. The actual drainage restriction could be ordered now under the officer's existing duty without claiming every downstream loss already proved its cause.

canal_p16_067.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_067.text: Luo received the inspection's public portions and kept the reply beside the finding. The gardener wanted the added stack named at the hearing. It would be, with the observed sequence and limited scope. Han said private builders sometimes read marks badly because clients asked them to finish quickly. The quarry owner did not need Han's general excuse; he needed to answer his own actual work. Yue put that sentence in the preparation note, then crossed out its sharpest wording before sending the question to the right receiver.

canal_p16_068.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_068.text: The public officer required the accessible outlet restored to its permitted current width under a checked sequence, with exposed work stopped if head changed. The quarry owner funded his own responsible crew and material through the accepted private work order. The canal's emergency allocation had closed and could not buy the correction a second time. Yue liked seeing a real order sent to somebody able to act on that ground. It did not pay every bean loss. It prevented the next ordinary shower from meeting exactly the same narrowed outlet.

canal_p16_069.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_069.text: Han's buyer agent arrived at the landing to watch the private goods loading preparation. He asked to look inside the public apparatus case because he wondered whether the stones had value toward the deposit. The case belonged to the commission and had never secured Han's private contract. Luo declined and showed the actual loading-gear security schedule he already held. The agent read it again and accepted the limit. Yue noticed how often an ordinary boundary had to be explained after a storm made every useful object look like available money.

canal_p16_070.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_070.text: Bao attended the counter from his supported chair for a brief light planning conversation he chose. His wrist had not improved enough for loaded work. The ordinary later repair receiver could revise final checking tasks after the clinician accepted them, leaving physical replacements to the actual qualified workers. He disliked watching others handle timber he could picture fixing. Tian brought the support strap he had ordered, fitted to the clinician's ordinary instruction. He paid the agreed private stitching price and adjusted it carefully, admitting the useful cloth deserved less complaint than his idle hand.

canal_p16_071.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_071.text: On the thirty-ninth morning, Yue rehearsed the hearing's current sequence with Pei and the clerk. They would state actual aid and payments, then hear direct losses, broader work consequences and unresolved cause questions under their own proper decisions. The old completed pledge would not reopen because repair and relief cost money. The valid fifty-six loan would not vanish because Han reimbursed one copper for a cart mistake. Yue read those facts once in plain words and stopped. The room needed people afterward, not a recitation that consumed all their time.

canal_p16_072.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_072.text: The gardener's daughter brought her current row-count copy and sat through the rehearsal without asking to speak for every family. She wanted her father to see where her earlier stick method joined the later actual plant count. Pei showed the two dated lines. The girl smiled, then asked whether the trustees would listen if her voice shook. Yue said the receiver could read her approved words if she wanted. The girl chose to try speaking first. The choice belonged to the person with the actual voice.

canal_p16_073.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_073.text: At the house beside the spill, the owner and tenant agreed on the direct private repairs already received and the household losses still offered for hearing. The earlier millet settlement stayed separate by its old date. The paid additional lodging was complete. The grandmother put the offered account inside her light sack, beside the painted cup only for the journey to the hearing. She wanted to take it out of the bag afterward. A departure plan had helped her leave; it did not need to become the permanent home of her ordinary papers.

canal_p16_074.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_074.text: The cooper's cart arrived at Han's high store late that afternoon for the next morning's booked delivery. Its load allowance fit the reserved hoist and four planks, and the driver read the actual upper road route. The goods stayed tagged until loading under the private plan. Han checked his thirty-two envelope and left it closed. Sixteen more would be needed after a real receiving inspection, not before. Yue watched him put both scheduled papers under their covers and hoped for an uncomplicated forty-first-day remittance without writing hope into the account.

canal_p16_075.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_075.text: At supper, Tian sang the known beginning of Qiao Lan's work song while threading the last stitch in her own paid order. She left its missing lines empty. Bao listened from his supported chair and said the pause sounded exactly long enough for a tired carpenter to swear. Pei laughed and admitted the old workers probably did. Yue laughed too, grateful for a history allowed to contain humor without concealing fatigue. The hearing tomorrow would be easier if its people remembered they had lives beyond whichever claim brought them together.

canal_p16_076.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_076.text: Before bed, Yue checked the orchard request's actual reply state. The matron had the proposed third morning after closure and Yue's offered full review interval. Acceptance still awaited the staff and patient schedule. Her personal wage tally could fund the priced ordinary journey once that answer came. Any visit owed under the actual earlier arrangement remained unfulfilled. She closed the message page without pretending an honest request deserved an immediate yes. Tomorrow's hearing would teach the same patience through questions much closer to the canal.

canal_p16_077.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_077.text: The fortieth morning's chairs were arranged beside the repaired gate, with the lower loss maps and private delivery note kept at different tables. The cooper's cart would go by the checked upper route while the public hearing began. Yue set the gardener's daughter's stool where she could reach the offered row sketch. Han waited with his conditional receiving paper and the valid claim copy. A bargain with the wharf was approaching, but first the bank would hear what its useful common water had cost the people who kept living beside it.

canal_p16_078.speaker: narrator
canal_p16_078.text: Before the chair called the hearing open, the gardener's daughter asked Yue whether she could keep her breakfast bun beside the row sketch. Pei found a clean little plate so crumbs would not hide the numbers. The girl said she might be less frightened after one more bite. Yue told her the chair had not started yet. She ate, then wiped her hands and held the approved paper. Around them, adults prepared losses worth many copper. This small real pause cost nothing the hearing needed to recover.
